- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for mean reversion or short-term rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or adjust downward by 2–5% in next period.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope or apply downward bias of 2–4% for next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates in early periods (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is positive; apply 1–3% downward correction for first 5 days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 75% of recent high), model tends to ignore it; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model often fails to capture short-term noise; use 1–2% smoothing filter or adjust based on 3-day moving average.
